chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab and Ibn Bukayr from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a Christian woman who was under a Christian man, and he divorced her; is there upon her a waiting period like the waiting period of a Muslim woman? He said, 'No, because the People of the Book are slaves/dependents of the Imam. Do you not see that they pay the jizya, just as the slave pays the tax to his masters?'
He said, 'And whoever among them converts to Islam, he is free, and the jizya is lifted from him.'

I said to him, 'And if she converts after he has divorced her, what is her waiting period if the Muslim man wishes to marry her?' He said, 'If she converts after he has divorced her, her waiting period is the waiting period of a Muslim woman.'

I said, 'And if he dies while she is Christian and he is Christian, and a Muslim man wishes to marry her?' He said, 'The Muslim man does not marry her until she observes a waiting period from the Christian of four months and ten days, which is the waiting period of a Muslim woman whose husband has died.'

I said to him, 'How is her waiting period when he divorces her made like that of the slave woman, and her waiting period when he dies made like that of the free Muslim woman, while you mention that they are slaves/dependents of the Imam?' He said, 'Her waiting period in divorce is not like her waiting period when her husband dies.'
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a Christian woman divorced by her Christian husband according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the distinct legal status of *Ahl al-Kitab* (People of the Book) as 'slaves of the Imam' (*mamalik lil-imam*), evidenced by their payment of *jizya* analogous to a slave's tribute. This theological premise explains the jurisprudential nuance where their *iddah* varies by circumstance: it is shorter upon divorce (like a slave) but extends to four months and ten days upon the husband's death (like a free woman), ensuring clarity for Muslim suitors.
